selected_layouts.source_locator: Figure 6P-10, MUTCD 11th Edition PDF pages 918–919; TA-10 general notes and diagram
matched_scene_facts: Urban two-way roadway with one apparent lane in each direction
One opposing-direction lane is closed and the ego-direction lane remains open
Channelizing devices form a longitudinal separation and taper
Work duration is less than three days
conflicting_scene_facts: TA-10 depicts a lane closure on a two-lane road using flaggers and therefore presumes alternating one-way traffic through the remaining lane; the scene explicitly does not establish an alternating-traffic operation or flaggers

selected_layouts.source_locator: Figure 6P-8, MUTCD 11th Edition PDF pages 914–915; Road Closure with an Off-Site Detour
matched_scene_facts: Opposing traffic is expected to detour
The work zone is near an intersection
conflicting_scene_facts: TA-8 depicts a road closure with an off-site detour, while only the opposing-direction lane is confirmed closed and the actual detour route and detour signing are unconfirmed

missing_scene_fields: Confirmed traffic-control method for opposing traffic (alternating one-way operation, full directional detour, or another control method)
Confirmed opposing-traffic detour route and associated detour signing
Whether the roadway configuration is actually one lane in each direction throughout the TTC zone
Whether the intersection approach or only the opposing lane is closed
stage0.selection_reason: The manual evidence identifies TA-10 as the closest two-lane lane-closure application, but its flagger/alternating-traffic arrangement conflicts with the explicit scene constraint that alternating traffic must not be inferred. TA-8 addresses a full road closure with an off-site detour, but the scene confirms only closure of the opposing-direction lane and does not confirm the detour route or control devices. Because the primary routing/control condition determines which mutually exclusive Typical Application applies, no primary TA can be selected without guessing.
